The condition $f(a,b,c)=\frac{f(a+1,b,c)+f(a-1,b,c)}{2}$ says that $f(a+1,b,c)-f(a,b,c)=f(a,b,c)-f(a-1,b,c)$. So for fixed $b,c$, $f$ is an affine function of $a$. The same holds in $b$ and in $c$ separately.

Applying this one variable at a time gives
$$f(a,b,c)=\sum_{i,j,k\in\{0,1\}} c_{ijk}\,a^i b^j c^k,$$
a multi-affine function with 8 free real coefficients. Conversely, every such function satisfies all three equations. The solution space therefore has dimension 8.

The values on the cube $\{0,1\}^3$ determine $f$ everywhere. Fixing $b,c\in\{0,1\}$, the values at $a=0,1$ determine $f(a,b,c)$ for all $a$. Doing this for each $(b,c)\in\{0,1\}^2$ gives $f$ on all lines in the $a$-direction through the cube. The same argument applied to $b$ and then to $c$ extends $f$ to all of $\mathbb{Z}^3$.

Fewer than 8 evaluations cannot work. The solution space has dimension 8, so 7 or fewer evaluations would leave a nonzero solution vanishing at all the chosen points, and $f$ would not be determined.

The minimum is therefore 8.

ANSWER: 8
